species.excerpt: A popular fancy goldfish variety with a distinctive double tail. Graceful swimmer that needs clean, cool water.
species.name: Fantail Goldfish

species.excerpt: A surface-dwelling fish with a distinctive hatchet-shaped body. Can leap from the water to catch insects. Needs a tight-fitting lid.
species.name: Hatchetfish

species.excerpt: A striking butterflyfish with a long snout for picking food from crevices. Beautiful but difficult to keep. May nip at corals.
species.name: Copperband Butterflyfish

species.excerpt: Ornamental carp bred for color and pattern. Hardy and long-lived. Primarily a pond fish but can be kept in very large indoor tanks.
species.name: Koi

species.excerpt: A large, colorful freshwater crayfish. Hardy and active. Will eat plants and may catch slow fish. Best kept alone or with fast tank mates.
species.name: Australian Redclaw Crayfish

species.excerpt: A selectively bred color variant of the freshwater angelfish with a striking marbled pattern of black, white, and silver. Classic centerpiece fish for community tanks.
species.name: Marble Angelfish

species.excerpt: Intelligent large cichlid. Can recognize owners. Very messy.
species.name: Oscar

species.excerpt: Colorful hawkfish. Perches on rocks. May eat small shrimp.
species.name: Flamehawkfish

species.excerpt: Emperor Snakehead is one of the largest and most impressive snakehead species, prized by advanced predatory fish keepers.
species.name: Emperor Snakehead

species.excerpt: Rainbow Snakehead (Channa pulchra) is a colorful medium-sized snakehead popular in predatory fish aquariums.
species.name: Rainbow Snakehead

species.excerpt: Sailfin Tang is one of the most recognizable tang species with its dramatic sail-like dorsal fin. An active herbivore for larger marine aquariums.
species.name: Sailfin Tang

species.excerpt: One of the most widespread clownfish species, adaptable to a wide range of conditions. Features yellow fins and dark bands, and readily hosts in many anemone species.
species.name: Clarkii Clownfish

species.excerpt: An iconic saltwater fish with a powder-blue body, white face, and bright yellow tail. Beautiful but prone to Ich; needs pristine water quality and a large tank.
species.name: Powder Blue Tang

species.excerpt: A recognizable butterflyfish with a dark raccoon-like mask across its eyes. Hardy for a butterflyfish but may nip at coral polyps in reef tanks.
species.name: Raccoon Butterflyfish

species.excerpt: A striking butterflyfish with an extremely elongated snout for picking small invertebrates from crevices. Can be finicky about feeding in captivity.
species.name: Longnose Butterflyfish

species.excerpt: A small, entertaining blenny with a dark front half and orange-yellow rear. Feeds on algae and is an excellent addition to reef tanks for algae control.
species.name: Bicolor Blenny

species.excerpt: A peaceful, slow-moving cardinalfish with red spots on its rear half and a dark vertical band. A mouthbrooder that is easy to care for in reef systems.
species.name: Pajama Cardinalfish

species.excerpt: Frogfish are masters of camouflage among marine aquarium fish. They use a lure to attract prey and can engulf fish nearly their own size.
species.name: Frogfish

species.excerpt: Ornate Bichir, one of the most colorful and sought-after bichir species. A primitive predatory fish with distinctive ornate patterning.
species.name: Ornate Bichir

species.excerpt: Delhezi Bichir, also called Armored Bichir, is a popular predatory fish with a distinctive pattern and robust body.
species.name: Delhezi Bichir

species.excerpt: Endlicheri Bichir is one of the larger bichir species, a powerful predator requiring spacious aquariums.
species.name: Endlicheri Bichir

species.excerpt: Red-tailed Catfish is one of the most iconic large predatory catfish, reaching over 1 meter. Requires very large systems or ponds.
species.name: Red-tailed Catfish

species.excerpt: Emperor Angelfish is one of the most iconic marine aquarium fish with striking adult coloration. juveniles look completely different with blue and white spirals.
species.name: Emperor Angelfish

species.excerpt: Porcupine Puffer is a charismatic marine pufferfish covered in spines. Known for inflating when threatened and for its expressive face.
species.name: Porcupine Puffer

species.excerpt: A stunning tang with a deep purple body and yellow tail, prized for algae control. Requires ample swimming space and a varied herbivorous diet.
species.name: Purple Tang

species.excerpt: A colorful wrasse with vibrant blue-green stripes and a distinctive tail pattern. Active and reef-safe, it helps control pyramid snails and small pests.
species.name: Melanurus Wrasse

species.excerpt: A dazzling wrasse known for its rapid fin-flashing display during courtship. Males display brilliant orange and blue colors, making them a reef tank showpiece.
species.name: Flasher Wrasse

species.excerpt: A hardy moray eel with a white body covered in dark snowflake-like spots. Generally reef-safe but may eat small fish and invertebrates it can fit in its mouth.
species.name: Snowflake Eel

species.excerpt: A colorful hawkfish with a distinctive arc-shaped marking around its eye and red-brown body stripes. Perches on coral heads and may eat small ornamental shrimp.
species.name: Arc-eye Hawkfish

species.excerpt: A beneficial sand-sifting goby that constantly filters sand through its mouth, keeping the substrate clean. Peaceful and excellent for reef aquariums.
species.name: Diamond Watchman Goby

species.excerpt: A gorgeous basslet with a deep purple body and black cap extending from head to dorsal fin. Shy but beautiful, prefers caves and overhangs in reef tanks.
species.name: Black Cap Basslet

species.excerpt: A stunning schooling anthias with vibrant orange-pink coloration. Males display a distinctive purple dorsal stripe; best kept in groups in reef aquariums.
species.name: Bartlett's Anthias

species.excerpt: One of the most popular Corydoras species, valued for its striking spotted pattern and ability to tolerate warmer water than most Corydoras, making it ideal for tropical community tanks.
species.name: Sterbai Corydoras

species.excerpt: A hardy, aggressive cichlid famous for being one of the easiest fish to breed in captivity. Its bold striped pattern and territorial behavior make it a fascinating species for dedicated tanks.
species.name: Convict Cichlid

species.excerpt: Often confused with the Rummy Nose Tetra, this species features a bright red head and striking black-and-white striped tail. A beautiful schooling fish for planted community tanks.
species.name: Firehead Tetra

species.excerpt: A small, shy labyrinth fish with a rich chocolate-brown body and yellow banding. One of the more challenging gouramis, requiring soft, acidic water and calm tankmates.
species.name: Chocolate Gourami

species.excerpt: A tiny, brilliantly colored fish with males displaying vivid red and blue vertical stripes. One of the smallest freshwater fish, ideal for nano tanks but can be territorial.
species.name: Scarlet Badis

species.excerpt: A tiny, charming goby with bold black and yellow banding resembling a bumblebee. Perfect for nano tanks, though they can be shy and prefer brackish or slightly brackish water.
species.name: Bumblebee Goby

species.excerpt: A stunning nano fish with bold black bands and a vibrant orange-red tail. One of the most colorful killifish, ideal for planted nano tanks and peaceful community setups.
species.name: Clown Killifish

species.excerpt: A dramatic marine fish with venomous spines and flowing red-and-white striped fins. Popular for its stunning appearance but venomous spines require careful handling.
species.name: Lionfish

species.excerpt: A large, stunning pleco with bold white stripes on a dark body. Known for its wood-eating behavior — must have driftwood in the tank for proper digestion.
species.name: Royal Pleco

species.excerpt: A small, spotted pleco with a distinctive leopard-like pattern. Hardy and adaptable, making it a good choice for intermediate pleco keepers.
species.name: Leopard Frog Pleco

species.excerpt: A tiny, shy labyrinth fish with subtle brown and orange banding. Requires very soft, acidic water and dense planting. A specialist species for experienced keepers.
species.name: Licorice Gourami

species.excerpt: A unique, dark brown fish with an elongated snout used to probe substrate for food. Uses weak electrical fields to navigate and communicate in murky water.
species.name: Elephantnose Fish

species.excerpt: A bold, colorful Central American cichlid with iridescent blue-green spots on a dark body. Named for its aggressive temperament. Hardy and visually striking.
species.name: Jack Dempsey

species.excerpt: The Peaceful Betta — a wild-type betta with iridescent green and blue coloration. Unlike Betta splendens, males are generally peaceful with each other. Hardy and beautiful.
species.name: Betta Imbellis

species.excerpt: A mouthbrooding betta with a large head and warm orange-red coloration on males. One of the most prized wild bettas. Requires soft, acidic water and pristine conditions.
species.name: Betta Macrostoma

species.excerpt: An ethereal, delicate rainbowfish with males displaying extraordinarily long, flowing dorsal and anal fin rays. Peaceful and graceful, best in species tanks or with similar gentle fish.
species.name: Threadfin Rainbowfish

species.excerpt: A tiny, brilliant blue-striped goby that acts as a cleaner fish on coral reefs. One of the few marine fish that readily accepts prepared foods. Ideal for nano reef tanks.
species.name: Neon Goby

species.excerpt: A small, hardy blenny with a distinctive dark spot at the base of the tail. Excellent algae grazer with an entertaining personality. Safe for reef tanks.
species.name: Tailspot Blenny

species.excerpt: The most effective algae-eating blenny for marine aquariums. Mottled brown camouflage pattern and distinctive bristly lips.Active and entertaining personality.
species.name: Lawnmower Blenny

species.excerpt: A small, reef-safe wrasse with a bright yellow body and distinctive eye stripe. Hunts flatworms and parasitic snails. Active swimmer that adds vibrant color to reef tanks.
species.name: Yellow Coris Wrasse

species.excerpt: A unique bottom-dwelling fish with a flattened body shaped like a suction cup, adapted to cling to rocks in fast-moving streams. Fascinating to watch and excellent algae grazers.
species.name: Hillstream Loach

species.excerpt: A slender dwarf cichlid with three dark horizontal stripes and blue-tinged fins. Males develop elongated fin extensions in mature tanks. Found in slow-moving streams across South America.
species.name: Three Stripe Dwarf Cichlid

species.excerpt: One of the most beautifully colored fish in the ocean, with psychedelic patterns of blue, orange, and green. Difficult to keep due to specialized diet of live copepods.
species.name: Mandarin Fish

species.excerpt: One of the smallest known fish species, reaching only 2 cm. A true nano fish for specialized planted tanks with soft, acidic water.
species.name: Pygmy Rasbora

species.excerpt: A peaceful dwarf cichlid named for the curved markings on its face that resemble a smile. One of the most docile cichlids, ideal for community planted tanks.
species.name: Smiling Cichlid

species.excerpt: The iconic "Dory" fish — a vibrant royal blue tang with a black palette marking and yellow tail. Demands large tanks with excellent water quality and strong flow.
species.name: Blue Tang

species.excerpt: A bright yellow goby that forms a symbiotic relationship with pistol shrimps. The shrimp digs and maintains a burrow while the goby stands guard. Fascinating behavioral display.
species.name: Yellow Watchman Goby

species.excerpt: A slender goby with a gradient from white to bright orange-red on the tail, and a distinctive elongated dorsal fin filament. Peaceful and hardy, perfect for nano reef tanks.
species.name: Firefish Goby

species.excerpt: One of the most affordable and hardy dwarf angelfish, with deep blue and orange-red vertical barring. Semi-reef-safe — may nip at large-polyp stony corals.
species.name: Coral Beauty Angelfish

species.excerpt: One of the hardiest and most colorful marine fish, with an electric blue body. Extremely tough and adaptable — ideal for cycling new marine tanks. Can be territorial.
species.name: Blue Devil Damselfish

species.excerpt: One of the most popular and colorful dwarf cichlids, with males displaying vibrant reds, blues, and yellows. Excellent centerpiece fish for planted South American biotope tanks.
species.name: Agassiz Dwarf Cichlid

species.excerpt: A small, active marine fish with six vibrant purple-pink horizontal lines on a orange body. Excellent reef inhabitant that hunts flatworms and parasitic snails.
species.name: Six Line Wrasse

species.excerpt: A stunning basslet with a bright purple front half fading to golden yellow on the rear. One of the most colorful and hardy marine aquarium fish, perfect for nano reef tanks.
species.name: Royal Gramma

species.excerpt: A tiny, brilliantly blue nano fish from the peat swamps of Borneo. One of the smallest aquarium fish, requiring soft, acidic water and careful maintenance.
species.name: Neon Blue Rasbora

species.excerpt: A small, colorful West African cichlid with males displaying blue and yellow patterns. Pairs form strong bonds and both parents guard the eggs.
species.name: Congo Dwarf Cichlid

species.excerpt: One of the most coveted and expensive aquarium fish, with bold black-and-white zebra striping. Endangered in the wild, captive-bred specimens are available.
species.name: Zebra Pleco

species.excerpt: A small, slender labyrinth fish with a pointed snout and subtle patterning. Hardy and adaptable, suitable for community tanks with soft to moderate water.
species.name: Spiketail Gourami

species.excerpt: A small, colorful labyrinth fish with males displaying blue-green iridescence. Peaceful and hardy, suitable for community planted tanks.
species.name: Sri Lanka Gourami

species.excerpt: A large, elegant South American cichlid that sifts substrate through its gills to find food. Peaceful for a cichlid, requiring sandy substrate and spacious tanks.
species.name: Eartheater Cichlid

species.excerpt: A small, colorful cichlid with a distinctive dark spot behind the ear and blue-tinged fins. Peaceful and active, suitable for community planted tanks.
species.name: Cupido Cichlid

species.excerpt: The world's smallest pufferfish, reaching only 2.5 cm. A fascinating, intelligent nano fish that hunts snails. Requires species-only or carefully selected tank mates.
species.name: Pea Puffer

species.excerpt: A striking freshwater fish with a sleek black body and vibrant red-orange fins. Active bottom-dweller that can be territorial. Best in spacious tanks with hiding spots.
species.name: Rainbow Shark

species.excerpt: A playful, social loach with a distinctive yoyo or almond-shaped pattern. Excellent snail hunter and bottom-dweller. Must be kept in groups of 5 or more.
species.name: Yoyo Loach

species.excerpt: A smaller, more iridescent relative of the Neon Tetra with a brilliant green-blue horizontal stripe. Peaceful nano fish for soft, acidic planted tanks.
species.name: Green Neon Tetra

species.excerpt: A majestic, slow-growing cichlid from Lake Tanganyika with bold black-and-white vertical stripes and a distinctive nuchal hump. One of the most iconic African cichlids.
species.name: Frontosa Cichlid

species.excerpt: The Cuckoo Catfish — a fascinating African catfish that is a natural brood parasite, laying its eggs in cichlid mouths. Hardy, active, and social bottom-dweller.
species.name: Synodontis Catfish

species.excerpt: A hardy labyrinth fish with striking blue and red coloration and flowing fins. One of the first tropical fish imported to Europe. Tolerates cooler temperatures than most tropicals.
species.name: Paradise Fish

species.excerpt: One of the few fish that reliably eats black beard algae (BBA). A sleek, active bottom-dweller with a distinctive horizontal black stripe. Best in groups.
species.name: Siamese Algae Eater

species.excerpt: A small tang with a distinctive dark body covered in fine yellow spots. One of the smallest tang species, ideal for mid-size reef tanks. Excellent algae grazer.
species.name: Kole Tang

species.excerpt: Beautiful South American cichlid with golden-green coloration.
species.name: Green Terror

species.excerpt: A small but striking snakehead with blue-green markings. Air-breathing predator that needs a secure lid and species-only tank.
species.name: Dwarf Snakehead

species.excerpt: A large, powerful predatory cichlid with a distinctive eyespot on the tail. Requires a very large tank and robust filtration.
species.name: Peacock Bass

species.excerpt: A colorful marine grouper with blue spots. Shy but predatory. May eat smaller tank mates. Needs hiding spots.
species.name: Marine Betta

species.excerpt: A hardy livebearer available in many colors. Tolerates a wide range of water conditions. Breeds readily in captivity.
species.name: Molly

species.excerpt: Alligator Gar is one of the largest freshwater predators in North America, reaching over 2 meters. Requires pond-scale housing.
species.name: Alligator Gar

species.excerpt: Naso Tang, also known as Lipstick Tang, is a large graceful tang species popular in reef and FOWLR systems.
species.name: Naso Tang

species.excerpt: A bold and territorial clownfish known for its deep maroon color and white stripes. Often hosts in bubble-tip anemones and can be aggressive toward tankmates.
species.name: Maroon Clownfish

species.excerpt: A hardy clownfish species with a vibrant red-orange body and a single white head bar. One of the easier saltwater clownfish to keep in home aquariums.
species.name: Tomato Clownfish

species.excerpt: A Caribbean icon with vivid blue and yellow coloration and a distinctive blue-ringed eye spot. Grows large and may nip at corals in reef setups.
species.name: Queen Angelfish

species.excerpt: A specialized parasite-eating wrasse that sets up cleaning stations for other fish. Difficult to keep as it relies on parasites from tankmates for nutrition.
species.name: Cleaner Wrasse

species.excerpt: A distinctive hawkfish with a long pointed snout and red-and-white checkered pattern. Perches on gorgonians and may prey on small shrimp.
species.name: Longnose Hawkfish

species.excerpt: A large, powerful triggerfish with iridescent blue facial markings and a sturdy dorsal spine. Can be aggressive and may rearrange rockwork or eat invertebrates.
species.name: Queen Triggerfish

species.excerpt: A large pufferfish with white spots and radiating stripes resembling the American flag. Known to eat invertebrates and may nip at corals.
species.name: Stars and Stripes Puffer

species.excerpt: Care profile for Pygmy Corydoras (Corydoras pygmaeus): 2.5 cm adult size, 22–26°C, pH 5.5–7.5, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Pygmy Corydoras

species.excerpt: Care profile for Honey Gourami (Trichogaster chuna): 5 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 6–7.5, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Honey Gourami

species.excerpt: Care profile for Kubotai Rasbora (Microdevario kubotai): 2.2 cm adult size, 22–27°C, pH 6.5–7.5, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Kubotai Rasbora

species.excerpt: Care profile for Chili Rasbora (Boraras brigittae): 2 cm adult size, 23–27°C, pH 4–7, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: Chili Rasbora

species.excerpt: Care profile for Red Garra (Garra rufa): 12 cm adult size, 20–27°C, pH 6.5–8, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Red Garra

species.excerpt: Care profile for German Blue Ram (Mikrogeophagus ramirezi): 6 cm adult size, 26–29°C, pH 5.5–7, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: German Blue Ram

species.excerpt: Care profile for Golden Pencilfish (Nannostomus beckfordi): 6 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 5.5–7.5, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: Golden Pencilfish

species.excerpt: Care profile for Rummynose Tetra (Hemigrammus rhodostomus): 5 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 5.5–7.5, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: Rummynose Tetra

species.excerpt: Care profile for Silver Hatchetfish (Gasteropelecus sternicla): 6.5 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 6–7.5, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: Silver Hatchetfish

species.excerpt: Care profile for Emerald Betta (Betta smaragdina): 7 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 6–7.5, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Emerald Betta

species.excerpt: Care profile for Clown Pleco (Panaqolus maccus): 10 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 6.5–7.5, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Clown Pleco

species.excerpt: Care profile for Dubois’ Tropheus (Tropheus duboisi): 12 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 7.8–8.6, expert difficulty.
species.name: Dubois’ Tropheus

species.excerpt: Care profile for Flame Angelfish (Centropyge loricula): 12 cm adult size, 24–27°C, pH 8.1–8.4, intermediate difficulty.
species.name: Flame Angelfish

species.excerpt: Care profile for Percula Clownfish (Amphiprion percula): 8 cm adult size, 24–28°C, pH 8–8.4, beginner difficulty.
species.name: Percula Clownfish

species.excerpt: Hardy predatory fish requiring large setups. Not suitable for community tanks.
species.name: Asian Snakehead

species.excerpt: Small peaceful loach that eats snails. Best kept in groups.
species.name: Dwarf Chain Loach

species.excerpt: Hardy bichir species. Air-breathing, needs secure lid.
species.name: Senegal Bichir

species.excerpt: Peaceful cichlid with distinctive head shape.
species.name: Bucktooth Parrot

species.excerpt: Distinctive black and white cardinalfish. Mouthbrooder.
species.name: Banggai Cardinalfish

species.excerpt: Excellent algae eater. Venomous dorsal spines.
species.name: Foxface Rabbitfish

species.excerpt: The classic goldfish. Hardy, peaceful, and one of the most recognized aquarium fish worldwide. Needs more space than commonly assumed.
species.name: Common Goldfish

species.excerpt: Fancy goldfish with a distinctive head growth (wen). Elegant and popular, requires slightly more care than common goldfish.
species.name: Oranda Goldfish

species.excerpt: The King of Goldfish in Japan. A dorsal-less fancy variety with a rounded body and gentle disposition.
species.name: Ranchu Goldfish

species.excerpt: One of the smallest pencilfish. Peaceful nano species for soft, acidic planted tanks. Best kept in schools.
species.name: Dwarf Pencilfish

species.excerpt: A slender, elongated predatory cichlid from South America. Fast, agile hunter that needs plenty of swimming space.
species.name: Pike Cichlid

species.excerpt: A smaller, more manageable lionfish with venomous spines. Striking appearance with flowing fins. May eat small fish and shrimp.
species.name: Dwarf Lionfish

species.excerpt: A large, striking triggerfish with bold patterns. Powerful jaws can crush shells. May rearrange decorations and eat tank mates.
species.name: Clown Triggerfish

species.excerpt: A large eel with striking black-and-white stripes. Generally peaceful toward fish too large to eat. Needs plenty of hiding spots.
species.name: Zebra Moray Eel

species.excerpt: The classic orange clownfish made famous by animation. Hardy and reef-safe, can host anemones.
species.name: Ocellaris Clownfish

species.excerpt: A manageable pleco (up to 13 cm) that eats algae and fits most community tanks. Males grow bristly tentacles.
species.name: Bristlenose Pleco

species.excerpt: A striking blue-scaled cichlid that is relatively peaceful for its size, though territorial when breeding. An avid digger, so anchor plants well.
species.name: Blue Acara

species.excerpt: A stunning killifish with lyre-shaped fins. Best kept in a small, heavily planted tank.
species.name: Lyretail Killifish

species.excerpt: A colorful dwarf cichlid that forms harem groups. Territorial when breeding; best in a species or biotope tank.
species.name: Cockatoo Dwarf Cichlid

species.excerpt: A surface-hunting killifish with golden flanks and red fins. Not annual, quite hardy, but will eat any fish small enough to fit its mouth.
species.name: Golden Wonder Killifish

species.excerpt: Arapaima (Hai Tuong Long) is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, reaching over 2 meters. Requires pond-scale or public aquarium housing.
species.name: Arapaima

species.excerpt: A large, silver schooling fish with black-edged fins. Despite its shark-like appearance, the Bala Shark is a gentle giant requiring spacious quarters.
species.name: Bala Shark

species.excerpt: One of the most popular aquarium fish, known for flowing fins and labyrinth breathing. Best kept alone or with peaceful tankmates.
species.name: Siamese Fighting Fish

species.excerpt: A stunning dark-bodied arowana that changes color with maturity. A surface-dwelling predator that needs very tall tanks and a tightly sealed lid.
species.name: Black Arowana

species.excerpt: A nocturnal fish that uses weak electrical fields to navigate. Its undulating anal fin allows graceful, silent movement in any direction.
species.name: Black Ghost Knifefish

species.excerpt: A distinctive fancy goldfish with protruding telescopic eyes and a matte black body. Gentle and slow-moving, best kept with similarly slow tankmates.
species.name: Black Moor Goldfish

species.excerpt: A beautiful black-and-gold loach that lives for a decade or more. Needs sand substrate to protect its barbels and a group of 5 or more.
species.name: Zebra Loach

species.excerpt: Coldwater classic. Fancy varieties need more space and better filtration than common goldfish — 150 L+ for a single adult.
species.name: Fancy Goldfish

species.excerpt: Not a true rasbora but a small danio from the cool, alkaline waters of Lake Inle. Unusual for a nano fish: it needs neutral-to-alkaline water.
species.name: Emerald Dwarf Rasbora

species.excerpt: A peaceful, schooling damselfish that adds shimmering movement to a reef tank.
species.name: Green Chromis

species.excerpt: Playful, social loach with striking orange-black stripes. Grows to 30 cm and needs a very large group.
species.name: Clown Loach

species.excerpt: A large, silver fish with distinctive spots and an undulating anal fin. A powerful predator that uses weak electrical discharges to navigate and hunt.
species.name: Clown Knifefish

species.excerpt: One of the hardiest and most popular catfish for community tanks. Forages the substrate in groups; sand is the ideal substrate.
species.name: Bronze Corydoras

species.excerpt: A charming armored catfish that scavenges the substrate. Peaceful and social, great for community tanks.
species.name: Peppered Corydoras

species.excerpt: A beloved black-and-white Cory that prefers cooler water than most tropical fish. Peaceful and perfect for planted tanks.
species.name: Panda Corydoras

species.excerpt: Most 'Julii Cory' sold in stores are actually this species. A lovely shoaling catfish with three dark lines along the flanks.
species.name: Three-Lined Corydoras

species.excerpt: A tiny, stunning fish covered in galaxy-like spots. Shy and needs a planted, dimly lit tank.
species.name: Celestial Pearl Danio

species.excerpt: An energetic, hardy fish with horizontal stripes. A great beginner species that thrives in cooler water.
species.name: Zebrafish

species.excerpt: Known as the Roseline Shark, this colorful barb features a distinctive red stripe. An active, peaceful schooling fish for larger community tanks.
species.name: Denison Barb

species.excerpt: A charming brackish puffer with distinctive markings. Needs hard-shelled foods to wear down its beak-like teeth; excellent personality for its size.
species.name: Figure-8 Puffer

species.excerpt: A fascinating bottom-dwelling ray from South American rivers. Requires a sandy substrate and excellent water quality; venomous barb on its tail.
species.name: Freshwater Stingray

species.excerpt: A large, fast-swimming schooling fish with iridescent blue stripes. Hardy and active, making it an excellent choice for beginner community setups.
species.name: Giant Danio

species.excerpt: Hardy tetra with a distinctive black body and flowing fins. Peaceful but may nip fins of slow tankmates.
species.name: Black Skirt Tetra

species.excerpt: A slender surface-dwelling fish with an elongated lower jaw. Hardy and fascinating to observe, though males can be territorial with each other.
species.name: Halfbeak

species.excerpt: A tiny, glowing orange tetra that adds brilliant color to nano and planted tanks. Peaceful and hardy, best kept in a group of 8 or more.
species.name: Ember Tetra

species.excerpt: A vivid red tetra that may nip fins unless kept in a large group of at least 12. Very active and hardy once settled.
species.name: Serpae Tetra

species.excerpt: A calm, hardy tetra with a bold neon stripe contrasting a dark body. Ideal for peaceful community tanks.
species.name: Black Neon Tetra

species.excerpt: A graceful dark tetra with elegant fins; males flare their dorsal in display. Hardy and perfect for peaceful planted tanks.
species.name: Black Phantom Tetra

species.excerpt: A gentle, schooling tetra with translucent yellow fins and lemon-tinted body. Great for planted community aquariums.
species.name: Lemon Tetra

species.excerpt: Grows much larger than most expect (30+ cm). Needs a very large tank; consider a dwarf species for smaller setups.
species.name: Common Pleco

species.excerpt: A massive schooling catfish often sold small but reaching over a meter. Despite its peaceful nature, its enormous adult size makes it suitable only for very large systems.
species.name: Iridescent Shark

species.excerpt: A powerful Central American predator cichlid with spotted markings resembling a jaguar. Extremely aggressive and territorial; best kept alone or with equally robust tankmates.
species.name: Jaguar Cichlid

species.excerpt: A truly transparent catfish that is shy unless kept in a group of 6 or more. Needs gentle flow and a dimly lit, mature tank.
species.name: Glass Catfish

species.excerpt: The famous yellow 'Yellow Lab' from Lake Malawi. One of the most peaceful mbuna; keep one male with several females.
species.name: Electric Yellow Cichlid

species.excerpt: A slender, prehistoric predator with an elongated snout full of needle-like teeth. An ambush hunter that can grow over a meter long.
species.name: Longnose Gar

species.excerpt: Known for a striking blue-to-orange gradient body. Needs a roomy tank and a group to look its best.
species.name: Boesemani Rainbowfish

species.excerpt: A vivid blue-and-red rainbowfish that stays small. Active open-water swimmer — needs a longer tank and a shoal of at least 8.
species.name: Dwarf Neon Rainbowfish

species.excerpt: A bold, brightly colored cichlid known for its impressive nuchal hump. Highly aggressive and territorial, demanding a species-only or carefully planned predator setup.
species.name: Midas Cichlid

species.excerpt: A hardy, peaceful dwarf cichlid that sifts sand for food. More tolerant of cooler water and varied chemistry than the Blue Ram.
species.name: Bolivian Ram

species.excerpt: A striking tetra with an extended, three-pronged tail in males. Males establish mild territories, so a roomy, planted tank suits them best.
species.name: Emperor Tetra

species.excerpt: A powerful South American predator cichlid prized for sport fishing. Colorful and active, but requires very large tanks and can bully smaller tankmates.
species.name: Orinoco Peacock Bass

species.excerpt: The Silver Arowana (Ngan Long) is one of the largest commonly kept freshwater aquarium fish, reaching up to 1 meter. A surface-dwelling predator requiring extremely large systems.
species.name: Silver Arowana

species.excerpt: Small algae-eating catfish that is the perfect cleanup crew for planted tanks. Needs established algae or supplemental food.
species.name: Otocinclus Catfish

species.excerpt: Eel-like, nocturnal loach that loves hiding among plants and driftwood. Peaceful scavenger.
species.name: Kuhli Loach

species.excerpt: Brighter and larger than the neon tetra. Prefers soft, slightly acidic blackwater conditions.
species.name: Cardinal Tetra

species.excerpt: A classic schooling tetra with a bright blue-red stripe. Hardy, peaceful and ideal for community tanks.
species.name: Neon Tetra

species.excerpt: A beautiful West African dwarf cichlid and one of the best beginner cichlids. Provide caves; pairs become territorial when breeding.
species.name: Kribensis

species.excerpt: A hardy, active barb that tolerates cooler water and is even kept as a pond fish in mild climates. Best in schools of 5 or more.
species.name: Rosy Barb

species.excerpt: A small, strikingly striped barb with a red-gold blaze. Peaceful and ideal for planted community aquariums.
species.name: Odessa Barb

species.excerpt: A large, shimmering tetra with rainbow reflections on mature males. Needs a spacious tank and a shoal to display its best colors.
species.name: Congo Tetra

species.excerpt: An active, spotted catfish with long barbels and an energetic personality. Best kept in groups; may eat small tankmates due to its predatory nature.
species.name: Pictus Catfish

species.excerpt: Colorful, active livebearer that is extremely easy to breed. Tolerates a wide range of water conditions.
species.name: Guppy

species.excerpt: A versatile livebearer that tolerates hard, even brackish water. Males reach 8 cm while females can grow to 12 cm.
species.name: Short-finned Molly

species.excerpt: A tiny, dazzling livebearer closely related to the guppy. Avoid keeping it with guppies, as the two species hybridize freely.
species.name: Endler's Livebearer

species.excerpt: A reef planktivore that needs frequent small feedings. Groups with one dominant male.
species.name: Lyretail Anthias

species.excerpt: An aggressive African cichlid that needs a hard, alkaline Malawi tank. Not for beginners or community tanks.
species.name: Zebra Mbuna Cichlid

species.excerpt: Graceful, tall-bodied cichlid. Semi-aggressive when breeding; pairs may defend territory.
species.name: Angelfish

species.excerpt: An iconic striped barb with a reputation for fin nipping — avoid it with long-finned fish unless kept in a group of 8 or more.
species.name: Tiger Barb

species.excerpt: A shy, peaceful barb that shows intense red color when happy. Great for planted aquariums.
species.name: Cherry Barb

species.excerpt: Red-bellied Piranha, the most well-known piranha species. A schooling predator that requires secure housing and careful handling.
species.name: Red-bellied Piranha

species.excerpt: A large, round-bodied fish with human-like teeth designed for crushing nuts and seeds. Often confused with piranhas but primarily herbivorous as an adult.
species.name: Red-Bellied Pacu

species.excerpt: A fiery-red Central American cichlid with a feisty personality. Extremely aggressive toward tankmates and known for rearranging aquarium decor.
species.name: Red Devil Cichlid

species.excerpt: A striking freshwater shark with a vibrant red tail. Semi-aggressive and best kept with robust tankmates in a well-planted aquarium.
species.name: Red-Tail Shark

species.excerpt: A classic fancy goldfish with a pronounced hump behind the head and flowing fins. Elegant and hardy, suitable for intermediate keepers.
species.name: Ryukin Goldfish

species.excerpt: A large algae-eating pleco with a distinctive sail-like dorsal fin. Hardy and effective at controlling algae, but grows very large for most home aquariums.
species.name: Sailfin Pleco

species.excerpt: The Asian Arowana, also known as Dragon Fish or Red/Golden Arowana (Huyet Long/Kim Long), is one of the most prized freshwater aquarium fish. A large, powerful predator requiring very large systems.
species.name: Asian Arowana

species.excerpt: Jardini Arowana, also known as Australian Arowana, is a smaller species of arowana suitable for large predator aquariums.
species.name: Jardini Arowana

species.excerpt: Black Piranha is a large, solitary piranha species. One of the most predatory freshwater fish kept in aquariums.
species.name: Black Piranha

species.excerpt: A relatively peaceful South American cichlid with a tall, disc-shaped body. Known for intelligent behavior and occasional plant-digging habits.
species.name: Severum

species.excerpt: A prehistoric-looking fish with a long, toothy snout and armored body. An ambush predator that requires large, open swimming space and a secure lid.
species.name: Spotted Gar

species.excerpt: A hardy, aggressive predator capable of breathing air. Requires a secure tank and should be kept alone or with carefully selected robust tankmates.
species.name: Spotted Snakehead

species.excerpt: The king of the aquarium — demanding stable warm water and high-quality food. Very rewarding for experienced keepers.
species.name: Discus

species.excerpt: A fancy goldfish variety featuring prominent protruding eyes. Available in many colors, this gentle fish requires careful tankmate selection.
species.name: Telescope Goldfish

species.excerpt: Named for the fiery red throat it flares during display. Robust and adaptable, but an avid digger — use sand and anchored decor.
species.name: Firemouth Cichlid

species.excerpt: The largest of the peacock bass species, a formidable apex predator. Incredibly powerful and aggressive; requires massive aquariums with robust filtration.
species.name: Three-Barred Peacock Bass

species.excerpt: A spectacular large catfish with tiger-like striping and a flattened snout. A powerful predator that can reach 1 meter; requires an enormous tank.
species.name: Tiger Shovelnose Catfish

species.excerpt: A shiny, active schooling fish that can grow quite large. Hardy and beginner-friendly but needs a big tank due to its adult size.
species.name: Tinfoil Barb

species.excerpt: A small labyrinth fish with beautiful red-blue stripes. Hardy but prone to stress in poor water conditions.
species.name: Dwarf Gourami

species.excerpt: A peaceful labyrinth fish dusted with pearl-like spots. Adaptable to varied water, but enjoys floating plants and gentle filtration.
species.name: Pearl Gourami

species.excerpt: The hardy 'Blue Gourami', available in many color morphs. Males can be aggressive with each other; a good snail-control fish.
species.name: Three-Spot Gourami

species.excerpt: A tiny croaking gourami that fits nano planted tanks. Excellent jumper — a tight lid and floating plants are essential.
species.name: Sparkling Gourami

species.excerpt: A small, peaceful rasbora with a copper-orange body and a lambchop-shaped black patch. Perfect for nano planted tanks.
species.name: Lambchop Rasbora

species.excerpt: A peaceful, hardy schooling fish with a distinctive black triangle marking. Ideal for planted community tanks.
species.name: Harlequin Rasbora

species.excerpt: A hardy air-breathing catfish capable of moving over land. An aggressive predator that can escape poorly covered tanks; best kept in species-only setups.
species.name: Walking Catfish

species.excerpt: A primitive, eel-like fish with dorsal finlets running along its back. A nocturnal predator that can breathe atmospheric air through a modified swim bladder.
species.name: Weeks Bichir

species.excerpt: One of the most aggressive freshwater fish, the Wolf Cichlid is a fearsome predator reaching half a meter. Only for experienced aquarists with very large systems.
species.name: Wolf Cichlid

species.excerpt: Active livebearer named after the male's long sword-like tail. Very easy to keep and breed.
species.name: Swordtail

species.excerpt: A friendly, colorful livebearer that adapts to almost any community tank. Extremely easy to keep and breed.
species.name: Southern Platy

species.excerpt: A bright yellow surgeonfish that needs a very large tank and plenty of grazing rock.
species.name: Yellow Tang

plant.name: Rotala sp. h'ra

plant.excerpt: A delicate stem plant with thin, needle-like leaves that turn deep red under high light. Also known as Needle Leaf Ludwigia, it adds fine texture and vibrant color to aquascapes.

plant.name: Frogbit

plant.excerpt: The smallest flowering plant — a tiny floating fern that doubles its coverage in days. Excellent nutrient absorber but extremely difficult to remove once established. Use with caution.
plant.name: Duckweed

plant.excerpt: A delicate aquarium moss with fine, triangular-shaped fronds that create a lush, textured carpet. Attaches readily to hardscape and is ideal for nano aquascapes.
plant.name: Taiwan Moss

plant.excerpt: A unique aquarium moss with fronds that droop downward, creating a distinctive weeping effect. Perfect for attaching to driftwood or rock overhangs for dramatic visual impact.
plant.name: Weeping Moss

plant.excerpt: A unique aquarium moss with upward-growing fronds that resemble flames. Creates a distinctive vertical texture different from traditional trailing mosses.
plant.name: Flame Moss

plant.excerpt: A miniature grass-like plant that forms a dense, low carpet. One of the smallest foreground plants, ideal for nano aquascapes. Tolerates low light but grows denser under high light.
plant.name: Lilaeopsis

plant.excerpt: A fast-growing, fern-like plant that can be floating or planted. Provides excellent cover for fry and absorbs nutrients rapidly. Very easy to grow.
plant.name: Water Sprite

plant.excerpt: One of the smallest aquarium plants, forming a dense carpet of tiny green leaves. Requires high light and CO2 to stay compact; Without it, stems stretch upward.
plant.name: Glossostigma

plant.excerpt: A floating plant that develops striking red roots and reddish leaf undersides under high light. Provides shade and natural algae control. Breeding ground for fry.
plant.name: Red Root Floater

plant.excerpt: A stunning red stem plant that turns deep crimson-red under high light and CO₂. One of the most beautiful red aquarium plants. Requires soft, slightly acidic water.
plant.name: Rotala Macrandra

plant.excerpt: A vivid red stem plant that maintains its intense red coloration even under moderate lighting. Hardy and fast-growing, making it accessible for intermediate aquascapers.
plant.name: Ludwigia Super Red

plant.excerpt: A floating rosette plant resembling small lettuce heads. Provides shade, absorbs excess nutrients, and offers cover for fry. Roots provide habitat for microorganisms.
plant.name: Dwarf Lettuce

plant.excerpt: A small floating fern with distinctive cup-shaped leaves. Fast-growing and excellent for nutrient吸收 in shrimp tanks. Does not reproduce as aggressively as duckweed.
plant.name: Salvinia

plant.excerpt: The most popular and hardy aquarium moss. Grows on almost any surface in almost any conditions. Versatile for attaching to driftwood, rocks, or creating moss walls.
plant.name: Java Moss

plant.excerpt: A rare, spherical green algae ball that grows extremely slowly. Requires almost no maintenance — just occasional squeezing and turning. A fascinating living decoration.

plant.name: Scarlet Temple

invertebrate.excerpt: A reef-safe detritivore that hides in live rock. Excellent cleanup crew member. Mostly nocturnal.
invertebrate.name: Brittle Star

invertebrate.excerpt: The most popular freshwater shrimp — bright red coloration, extremely hardy, and prolific breeder. The gateway species for shrimp keeping. Tolerates a wide range of conditions.
invertebrate.name: Cherry Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: The best algae-eating snail for aquariums. Cannot reproduce in freshwater, so populations stay stable. Comes in zebra, tiger, and olive patterns. Will lay white eggs on glass.
invertebrate.name: Nerite Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: One of the most beautiful but demanding anemones, with vibrant green or purple tentacles and a brightly colored oral disc. Requires intense lighting and stable water parameters.
invertebrate.name: Magnificent Anemone

invertebrate.excerpt: A distinctive starfish with dark brown tubercles resembling chocolate chips on a lighter body. Hardy but may consume corals and small invertebrates.
invertebrate.name: Chocolate Chip Starfish

invertebrate.excerpt: An attractive starfish with a geometric pattern of orange and cream plates. Generally reef-safe but may starve without adequate microfilm and detritus in the tank.
invertebrate.name: Fromia Starfish

invertebrate.excerpt: A conical-shaped algae-eating snail that is one of the most effective and hardy cleanup crew members for reef aquariums. Can right itself if overturned.
invertebrate.name: Trochus Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, cone-shaped snail that excels at consuming film algae from glass and rocks. Essential for reef tank maintenance but cannot right itself if flipped over.
invertebrate.name: Astraea Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A striking marine shrimp with white body and purple-magenta spots. Famous for eating starfish, including crown-of-thorns. Must be kept in pairs.
invertebrate.name: Harlequin Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, semi-terrestrial crab with striking purple coloration and bright yellow eyes. Requires a paludarium setup with both land and water areas.
invertebrate.name: Vampire Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: A large, striking freshwater snail with a conical shell and colorful body. Comes in orange, yellow, and dark variants. Active algae and detritus consumer, but slow breeder.
invertebrate.name: Rabbit Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A high-grade Caridina morph with bold black and white banding. One of the most prized ornamental shrimp. Requires soft, acidic water (pH 6.0-6.8, GH 4-6) and pristine conditions.
invertebrate.name: Taiwan Bee Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A striking blue color morph of Caridina cantonensis. Deep blue body with white banding. Extremely sensitive to water parameters — requires very soft, acidic water.
invertebrate.name: Blue Bolt Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, bright green marine crab valued for its ability to eat bubble algae (Valonia) in reef tanks. Generally peaceful but may eat small snails or corals.
invertebrate.name: Emerald Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: A small marine scavenger snail that burrows through sand, consuming detritus and leftover food. Essential for maintaining clean substrate in reef tanks.
invertebrate.name: Nassarius Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A large marine snail with a heavy, conical shell. One of the most effective algae grazers for reef tanks, capable of consuming large amounts of film and hair algae.
invertebrate.name: Turbo Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, bright red hermit crab that scavenges detritus and algae. One of the safest hermit crabs for reef tanks as it rarely attacks snails for shells.
invertebrate.name: Scarlet Hermit Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: A selectively bred color morph of Neocaridina davidi with solid, opaque blue coloration. Hardy and easy to breed, making them popular for planted tanks.
invertebrate.name: Blue Diamond Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A marine tube worm with a stunning feathery crown used for filter feeding. Retracts quickly when disturbed. Peaceful and easy to keep in reef tanks.
invertebrate.name: Feather Duster Worm

invertebrate.excerpt: A large, impressive freshwater shrimp with fan-like appendages used to filter feed from the current. Can grow up to 15 cm and requires strong water flow and clean, well-oxygenated water.
invertebrate.name: Vampire Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, colorful freshwater shrimp available in green, brown, and striped morphs. Hardy and easy to breed, making them excellent additions to planted community tanks.
invertebrate.name: Babaulti Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A selectively bred freshwater shrimp with striking deep blue coloration. Requires soft, acidic water and careful parameter maintenance. Prized by shrimp collectors.
invertebrate.name: Blue Tiger Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A selectively bred freshwater shrimp with opaque white coloration resembling snowballs. Requires soft, acidic water and pristine conditions for breeding.
invertebrate.name: Snowball Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A bright yellow color morph of Neocaridina davidi with a distinctive golden back stripe. Hardy, prolific breeder, and excellent algae consumer for planted tanks.
invertebrate.name: Golden Back Yellow Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A selectively bred color morph of the red swamp crayfish with brilliant blue coloration. Hardy and active, but will eat plants and harass tank mates.
invertebrate.name: Blue Crayfish

invertebrate.excerpt: A solid black color morph of Caridina cantonensis with minimal white markings. One of the rarest and most expensive shrimp variants. Requires expert-level water parameters.
invertebrate.name: King Kong Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A stunning red and white striped shrimp from the ancient lakes of Sulawesi, Indonesia. Unlike most Caridina, it thrives in warm, alkaline water (pH 7.5-8.5, 26-30°C).
invertebrate.name: Sulawesi Cardinal Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A stunning giant clam with brilliant blue, green, or purple mantle patterns. Photosynthetic — requires strong lighting. A showcase centerpiece for reef tanks.
invertebrate.name: Tridacna Maxima Clam

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, colorful shrimp from Sulawesi lakes. Red body with white markings. Needs warm, hard water.
invertebrate.name: Caridina omnipos (Sulawesi Cardinal Shrimp)

invertebrate.excerpt: A detritivore that processes sand and waste. Reef-safe but needs established tank. Can be sensitive to water changes.
invertebrate.name: Sea Cucumber

invertebrate.excerpt: A hardy host anemone with long tentacles tipped in white or purple. Commonly paired with clownfish and thrives under moderate to high lighting.
invertebrate.name: Sebae Anemone

invertebrate.excerpt: A tiny, fascinating crab that carries small anemones in its claws like pom-poms for defense and food capture. Harmless and entertaining in reef aquariums.
invertebrate.name: Pom-Pom Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: A large urchin with thick, blunt spines resembling pencils. An excellent algae grazer that may inadvertently knock over small corals or unsecured rockwork.
invertebrate.name: Pencil Urchin

invertebrate.excerpt: The striped predator of the aquarium world, kept to hunt down pest snails and worms. It burrows by day and hunts by night, and will happily share a tank with fish and plants - it ignores shrimp and fish entirely. Also known as Clea helena; both names are accepted.
invertebrate.name: Assassin Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A burrowing starfish that churns the sand bed and feeds on worms, copepods, and small benthic invertebrates living in it. Demands a deep (7 cm+), well-established sand bed and roughly 280 L per specimen; once it exhausts the sand's food supply it quietly starves, so it suits mature systems only.
invertebrate.name: Sand-Sifting Starfish

invertebrate.excerpt: Also called the wood shrimp, it stations itself in the current and fans microscopic food from the water with its four feathery feeding fans. Needs brisk flow (8-10x tank volume per hour) and regular feedings of powdered or micro food, or it will slowly starve in a clean tank.
invertebrate.name: Bamboo Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A high-grade bee shrimp bred for its striking white-and-red pattern. Demanding keeper: thrives only in soft, acidic water (GH 4-6 dGH) and practically requires reverse-osmosis water with an active buffering substrate. Stable cool temperatures around 22 C are essential.
invertebrate.name: Crystal Red Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: The classic algae-eating workhorse shrimp, unmatched for clearing hair algae from planted tanks. Hardy at 3-15 dGH, but never breeds in freshwater: its larvae need brackish water, so all reports of 'Amano babies' in freshwater tanks are actually other shrimp species.
invertebrate.name: Amano Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: The classic clownfish host anemone whose tentacle tips swell into bubbles when healthy. Demands bright light (350-500 PAR) and a stable, mature 115 L+ reef; anchor its foot in a rock crevice, not open sand, target-feed it meaty food, and keep corals clear of its stinging reach.
invertebrate.name: Bubble-Tip Anemone

invertebrate.excerpt: A pea-sized, fully aquatic crab - no land zone needed - that perches on driftwood and picks microparticles from the water. Fragile and easily overlooked; keep a group of 3 or more in a mature nano tank, and never expose it to copper or sharp parameter swings.
invertebrate.name: Thai Micro Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: The famous skunk cleaner shrimp that runs a cleaning station: fish line up to have parasites and dead skin picked off. Hardy, outgoing, and reef-safe; an Atlantic lookalike, Lysmata grabhami, is sold under the same name in some regions.
invertebrate.name: Cleaner Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A deep blood-red cleaner shrimp that treats fish at a personal cleaning station. More shy and nocturnal than its cousins and noticeably pricey; needs a stable, mature reef and is extremely sensitive to copper - remove it before any copper-based treatment.
invertebrate.name: Fire Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: Nature's aiptasia control: it hunts and eats the glass anemones that plague reef tanks. Forgiving of typical reefkeeper mistakes and tolerant of various foods, but as an invertebrate it is highly sensitive to copper. Check the stripe pattern - the similar camel shrimp stays a pest-eater only in name.
invertebrate.name: Peppermint Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A conically shelled burrower that aerates the substrate and patrols it for leftover food at night. Females reproduce by parthenogenesis, so a single snail can seed a colony - they are a genuine muck-prevention asset, but heavy feeding will let them multiply fast.
invertebrate.name: Malaysian Trumpet Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A tidy, reef-safe urchin dressed in alternating dark and light bands that keeps rock, glass, and decor swept of algae and film. Grazes mostly at night and stays put by day; supplement with nori in low-algae tanks and never expose it to copper or high nitrate.
invertebrate.name: Tuxedo Urchin

invertebrate.excerpt: A tiny, vivid red dwarf shrimp that breeds easily and endlessly entertains. Fine in nano tanks from 20 L; keep GH 4-15 dGH for successful molting, avoid copper-based medications entirely, and use a sponge filter so young shrimplets never get sucked in.
invertebrate.name: Red Cherry Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A see-through, feather-light scavenger sold by the handful. Tough across 3-15 dGH and a wide temperature band. Beware mislabeled tankmates: true Ghost Shrimp is Palaemon paludosus, while the larger, more predatory Macrobrachium species are often sold under the same name.
invertebrate.name: Ghost Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A charismatic crab with vivid red claws that needs brackish water (SG 1.003-1.010) plus a 50-70% land area to climb on - it is not a true freshwater species despite how stores sell it. Feisty with slow tankmates; keep one per tank and cover every escape route.
invertebrate.name: Red Claw Crab

invertebrate.excerpt: A Caribbean anemone in a dazzling range of colors that, unlike most anemones, settles where placed and rarely wanders. Hardy and forgiving, it anchors its foot in the sand or rock and accepts meaty foods; keep small corals out of reach of its stinging tentacles. Often sold as Epicystis crucifer.
invertebrate.name: Rock Flower Anemone

invertebrate.excerpt: The large, coiled ramshorn that doubles as a cleanup crew and a living water-quality alarm. Every individual is hermaphroditic, so any pair can breed - populations explode only when overfeeding creates a feast, and they shrink right back once feeding is cut back.
invertebrate.name: Great Ramshorn Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A colorful, active apple snail that cruises the glass for algae and leftover food. Pairs lay their pink egg clutches above the waterline - remove them to avoid overpopulation. Keep hardness at 7-18 dGH and offer calcium-rich foods so the shell stays strong.
invertebrate.name: Mystery Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A bold, long-antennaed shrimp with coral bands that stands guard at its cave and makes an instant display piece. Not a true shrimp (it belongs to Stenopodidea): keep it singly or as a mated pair, as it will attack other crustaceans in its territory.
invertebrate.name: Coral Banded Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A striped, hard-working algae grazer that never overpopulates: its eggs are laid all over the glass but only hatch in brackish water, so they simply stay put. Prefers harder water (GH 6-20 dGH) with calcium for a healthy shell; watch for escapes, as it can climb out of open tanks.
invertebrate.name: Zebra Nerite Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A striking red shrimp from Lake Matano in Sulawesi. Requires warm, alkaline water. More challenging than Neocaridina.
invertebrate.name: Sulawesi Red Cherry Shrimp

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, useful cleanup crew snail. Burrows in sand, consumes algae and detritus. Hardy and reef-safe.
invertebrate.name: Cerith Snail

invertebrate.excerpt: A small, translucent shrimp that lives on sea anemones. Fascinating symbiotic relationship. Reef-safe.
invertebrate.name: Sexy Anemone Shrimp

coral.excerpt: Non-photosynthetic soft coral. Extremely challenging.
coral.name: Dendronephthya

coral.excerpt: A popular LPS coral with vivid, fleshy polyps. Available in many colors. Moderate care requirements.
coral.name: Acan Lord

coral.excerpt: A large, solitary LPS coral with vivid fleshy polyps. One polyp per skeleton. Popular for its vibrant colors.
coral.name: Scolymia

coral.excerpt: A leather coral with finger-like projections. Hardy and fast-growing. Can release terpenes that irritate other corals.
coral.name: Sinularia Leather

coral.excerpt: A branching SPS coral that is one of the easiest Acroporidae to keep. Fast-growing and available in orange, purple, and green. Great entry point for SPS keeping.
coral.name: Montipora Digitata

coral.excerpt: Long, glassy tentacles with stinging power — give it plenty of distance from neighbors.
coral.name: Galaxea

coral.excerpt: A branching SPS that is hardy by acropora standards; brown bases with pink tips.
coral.name: Cauliflower Coral

coral.excerpt: Delicate thin branches that grow into a bird’s nest shape; strong sweeper tentacles at night.
coral.name: Bird’s Nest Coral

coral.excerpt: A hardy massive LPS with maze-like grooves; tolerant of less stable conditions.
coral.name: Honeycomb Brain Coral

coral.excerpt: Flamboyant tentacles with vivid tips; sensitive to water quality swings.
coral.name: Elegance Coral

coral.excerpt: A fleshy, colorful LPS that stays on the sand bed and tolerates feeding.
coral.name: Open Brain Coral

coral.excerpt: Fungia, also known as Plate Coral or Mushroom Coral, is a free-living LPS coral. A beautiful addition to reef tanks placed on the sand bed.
coral.name: Fungia Coral

coral.excerpt: A encrusting soft coral that forms a bright green mat of polyps that wave in the current. Fast-growing and very hardy, but can become invasive if not managed.
coral.name: Green Star Polyps

coral.excerpt: A colonial polyp coral closely related to Zoanthids, forming dense mats of brownish polyps. Very hardy and fast-growing, but some species contain palytoxin — handle with care.
coral.name: Palythoa

coral.excerpt: A large, fleshy LPS coral with a distinctive brain-like pattern. Available in vibrant reds, greens, and purples. Hardy and tolerant of varying conditions.
coral.name: Lobo Coral

coral.excerpt: An LPS coral with distinctive grape-like vesicles that inflate during the day and retract at night. Elegant and unique, suitable for intermediate reef keepers.
coral.name: Bubble Coral

coral.excerpt: A non-photosynthetic (NPS) LPS coral that must be target-fed. Produces beautiful translucent polyps in orange, yellow, or white. A showcase species for advanced reef keepers.
coral.name: Dendrophyllia Coral

coral.excerpt: One of the most sought-after LPS corals, featuring long flowing tentacles with bright tips that sway elegantly in the current. A centerpiece coral for reef tanks.
coral.name: Torch Coral

coral.excerpt: A flat, disc-shaped mushroom coral available in a stunning array of colors including blue, green, red, and purple. One of the hardiest and easiest corals to keep, perfect for beginners.
coral.name: Discosoma Mushroom

coral.excerpt: An LPS coral with trumpet-shaped polyps that extend feeding tentacles at night. Hardy and tolerant, making it suitable for beginners. Available in green, brown, and purple morphs.
coral.name: Trumpet Coral

coral.excerpt: A classic brain coral with a distinctive honeycomb pattern. Hardy LPS coral available in green, red, and purple. Night-feeding tentacles extend to capture food.
coral.name: Favia Brain Coral

coral.excerpt: A branching SPS coral with a distinctive fuzzy appearance from extended polyps. Hardy for an SPS coral, making it a good first Acropora-family species. Available in pink, purple, and brown.
coral.name: Stylophora Coral

coral.excerpt: An LPS coral with a distinctive plating or encrusting growth pattern and vibrant contrasting mouth and ridge colors. A highly prized collector coral.
coral.name: Chalice Coral

coral.excerpt: A hardy SPS coral with distinctive leaf-like or encrusting growth forms. Tolerates a wide range of conditions, making it a good beginner SPS coral. Available in green and brown.
coral.name: Pavona Coral

coral.excerpt: A large, textured mushroom coral with distinctive bumpy or ridged surface. Hardy and fast-spreading. Available in green, blue, and purple. Great for beginner reef tanks.
coral.name: Rhodactis Mushroom

coral.excerpt: A branching LPS coral with clusters of tentacles that resemble frog eggs. Available in green, pink, and purple color morphs. Moderate care requirements make it popular with intermediate reefers.
coral.name: Frogspawn Coral

coral.excerpt: A soft coral famous for its pulsing polyps that open and close rhythmically. One of the few corals that can be propagated easily by fragments. Excellent beginner reef coral.
coral.name: Xenia Coral

coral.excerpt: A fast-growing soft coral with tree-like branching structure. Known for its ability to shed its skin and relocate in the tank. Very hardy and beginner-friendly.
coral.name: Kenya Tree Coral

coral.excerpt: Non-photosynthetic coral. Needs direct feeding.
coral.name: Sun Coral

coral.excerpt: Orange non-photosynthetic coral. Needs regular feeding.
coral.name: Tubing Coral

coral.excerpt: A branching SPS coral also known as Cauliflower Coral. Relatively hardy for an SPS. Good for beginner SPS keepers.
coral.name: Pocillopora

coral.excerpt: Alveopora is a flower pot coral similar to Goniopora but with fewer tentacle pairs. A popular LPS coral for reef aquariums.
coral.name: Alveopora Coral

coral.excerpt: A low-light LPS with bubble-like polyps, suited to shaded areas.
coral.name: Blastomussa

coral.excerpt: Distinctive fleshy polyps on a branching skeleton; great first LPS.
coral.name: Candy Cane Coral

coral.excerpt: Long green tentacles with daisy-like tips; a hardy beginner LPS.
coral.name: Duncan Coral

coral.excerpt: The flower pot coral — challenging to keep long-term without diligent feeding.
coral.name: Goniopora

coral.excerpt: A non-photosynthetic sea fan requiring frequent target feeding.
coral.name: Gorgonian

coral.excerpt: Has sweeping tentacles that can sting neighbors — give it space.
coral.name: Hammer Coral

coral.excerpt: A hardy soft coral with a thick leather-like body and short polyps.
coral.name: Lobophytum Leather

coral.excerpt: Plate-forming SPS that grows quickly once established.
coral.name: Montipora Capricornis

coral.excerpt: A massive boulder coral with a calm growth form.
coral.name: Porites

coral.excerpt: Wavy, colorful mushrooms that are extremely hardy.
coral.name: Ricordea Mushroom

coral.excerpt: A demanding SPS coral requiring pristine water and stable parameters.
coral.name: Staghorn Acropora

coral.excerpt: A classic table-shaped SPS coral forming wide flat colonies.
coral.name: Table Acropora

coral.excerpt: Soft coral that sheds skin and releases chemical warfare when stressed.
coral.name: Toadstool Leather

coral.excerpt: A plate-shaped LPS coral that thrives in lower light conditions.
coral.name: Turbinaria

coral.excerpt: Colorful colonial polyps that are very forgiving for new reef keepers.
coral.name: Zoanthids

coral.excerpt: A branching SPS coral with rounded tips. Hardy and fast-growing for an SPS. Available in pink, purple, and green.
coral.name: Cat's Paw Coral

equipment.excerpt: Full-spectrum LED light designed for planted aquariums. Provides optimal wavelengths for plant growth.
equipment.name: Planted LED Light

equipment.excerpt: High-output LED light designed for reef corals. Provides blue and white spectrum for coral growth and coloration.
equipment.name: Reef LED Light

equipment.excerpt: Programmable pump for automatic dosing of supplements, additives, or two-part solutions. Essential for reef tanks.
equipment.name: Dosing Pump

equipment.excerpt: Dissolves calcium carbonate media to maintain calcium and alkalinity levels in reef tanks. Essential for demanding SPS coral systems with high calcium consumption.
equipment.name: Calcium Reactor

equipment.excerpt: Measures water salinity by refracting light through a sample. More accurate and easier to use than hydrometers. Essential for marine aquarium keeping.
equipment.name: Refractometer

equipment.excerpt: A simple device for monitoring water temperature. Available as digital stick-on, glass, or digital probe types. Essential for maintaining stable conditions for tropical fish.
equipment.name: Aquarium Thermometer

equipment.excerpt: A chamber that forces water through filter media (carbon, GFO, biopellets) for enhanced chemical or biological filtration. Used in sump systems for advanced nutrient control.
equipment.name: Media Reactor

cons: Needs a bucket or drain nearby
equipment.excerpt: A siphon tool used to remove debris and waste from substrate during water changes. Essential for maintaining clean gravel and preventing anaerobic pockets.
equipment.name: Gravel Vacuum

cons: Must use with every water change
equipment.excerpt: A water conditioner that neutralizes chlorine, chloramine, and heavy metals from tap water. Essential for every water change to protect fish and beneficial bacteria.
equipment.name: Dechlorinator

equipment.excerpt: A submersible pump that creates oscillating water movement, simulating natural wave action. Essential for reef tanks to provide adequate flow for corals.
equipment.name: Wave Maker

cons: Not a substitute for water changes
equipment.excerpt: A chemical filtration media that removes dissolved organic compounds, medications, and yellowing agents from water. Used in canister filters, hang-on-back filters, and media reactors.
equipment.name: Activated Carbon

equipment.excerpt: Measures Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) to quantify light intensity for corals and plants. The most accurate way to compare and set aquarium lighting.
equipment.name: PAR Meter

equipment.excerpt: Active buffering substrates like ADA Amazonia, Tropica Soil, or Controsoil that lower pH and provide nutrients for planted tanks. Essential for soft-water plant setups.
equipment.name: Aquarium Soil Substrate

equipment.excerpt: Automates regular partial water changes by slowly draining and refilling water on a schedule. Reduces manual maintenance and maintains stable parameters.
equipment.name: Automatic Water Change System

equipment.excerpt: A handheld electronic device for precise pH measurement. More accurate than test kits but requires regular calibration and proper storage to maintain accuracy.
equipment.name: Digital pH Meter

cons: Not a replacement for full water test
equipment.excerpt: Measures Total Dissolved Solids in water, indicating overall water purity. Essential for RO/DI systems, shrimp keeping, and monitoring mineral content in planted tanks.
equipment.name: TDS Meter

equipment.excerpt: A submersible or external pump that returns filtered water from a sump back to the main tank. Critical component of sump-based filtration systems.
equipment.name: Return Pump

equipment.excerpt: A thermoelectric or compressor-based cooling device that maintains stable water temperature. Essential for marine tanks in warm climates and for temperature-sensitive species.
equipment.name: Aquarium Chiller

equipment.excerpt: A fine polyester padding used as mechanical filtration media to trap fine particles and polish water clarity. Placed as the final stage in canister or sump filtration.
equipment.name: Filter Floss

equipment.excerpt: A clip-on fan that cools water through evaporation. A cheaper alternative to a chiller for maintaining temperature in warm climates, though it increases evaporation.

equipment.excerpt: Automatically replenishes evaporated water with fresh or RO/DI water. Maintains stable salinity in marine tanks and stable water level in freshwater tanks.

equipment.excerpt: Passes aquarium water through UV light to kill parasites, bacteria, and algae spores. Effective against ich, velvet, and free-floating algae. Size determines kill rate.

equipment.excerpt: Precision digital aquarium heater with electronic thermostat. More accurate than traditional heaters.
equipment.name: Digital Heater

equipment.excerpt: Active substrate that lowers pH and provides nutrients for planted tanks. Essential for high-tech aquascaping.
equipment.name: Aquasoil Substrate

equipment.excerpt: Essential component for dissolving CO2 into aquarium water
equipment.name: CO2 Diffuser

equipment.excerpt: Visual indicator of CO2 levels in aquarium water
equipment.name: CO2 Drop Checker

equipment.excerpt: Traditional fluorescent lighting popular for reef and planted tanks
equipment.name: T5 Fluorescent Light

equipment.excerpt: Drives sponge filters, air stones and surface agitation. Useful for emergency oxygenation.
equipment.name: Air Pump

equipment.excerpt: An external filter with high media capacity and flexible hose routing. Best for medium to large planted tanks.
equipment.name: Canister Filter

equipment.excerpt: Provides water movement inside the tank. Essential for reef tanks and high-flow freshwater setups.
equipment.name: Circulation Pump (Powerhead)

equipment.excerpt: Regulates CO₂ from a cylinder into your planted tank via diffuser or inline reactor.

equipment.excerpt: A compact submersible filter that sits inside the tank. Good for small aquariums.
equipment.name: Internal Filter

equipment.excerpt: Energy-efficient lighting. For planted tanks, choose a fixture with full-spectrum LEDs and adjustable intensity.
equipment.name: LED Aquarium Light

equipment.excerpt: Liquid test kit for pH, ammonia, nitrite and nitrate. Essential for cycling and maintenance.
equipment.name: Master Test Kit

equipment.excerpt: An air-driven filter with a sponge media. Perfect for breeding tanks and shrimp setups.
equipment.name: Sponge Filter

equipment.excerpt: Thermostatically controlled heating for tropical tanks. Choose roughly 1 watt per liter of water.

equipment.excerpt: Removes dissolved organic waste from marine tanks via foam fractionation. Essential for reef systems.
equipment.name: Protein Skimmer

equipment.excerpt: Dispenses dry food on a timer while you are away. Choose one with a reliable mechanism and dry pellets.

equipment.excerpt: Inert gravel for freshwater tanks. Rinse thoroughly before use; depth of 2–5 cm suits most planted tanks.

equipment.excerpt: Pressurized container feeding CO₂ through a regulator into the planted tank. The reliable heart of a high-tech setup.
